title: Identification from First-Row Star Experiments in the Dense Confounded Row Gadget
banked_reason: The note proves a non-obvious all-rank binary-hub identification functional, but unresolved ID-ME capability and an unrepaired GID-PO comparator overreach leave it incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The no-exact-cover argument treats the raw star/triple gc-factor chunks as exhaustive, but GID-PO Algorithm 1 searches MVEFs for every target factor and source; audit all resulting candidate index sets (or narrow the claim) before asserting that GID-PO returns no formula and that this theorem strictly exceeds its criterion.
The comparator analysis stops after skipped EXPAND and the initial exact-cover obstruction, leaving every matrix-equation module that could synthesize the same identification unresolved.

The result is also confined to a specially structured star-plus-one-triple design, while its converse concerns one permitted alphabet specification and establishes neither designated-triple necessity nor a broader complete experiment calculus.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an explicit all-rank functional for the positive finite binary-hub star-plus-triple family, a branch-faithful adaptive rule using only stars in the cancellation branch, and positive R3 twins proving worst-case star-only nonidentification. The mathematics passed review, but the claimed GID-PO comparison did not audit MVEF-derived candidates and the stronger ID-ME separation would require a new uniform closure analysis across ID-RC, PROXY, CF-INV, and CF-INT. The sound structural results remain reusable, while comparator claims must be narrowed or independently completed.
tldr: All first-row star experiments plus one predesignated hub triple identify the full sink distribution of the positive dense confounded row SCM uniformly over every binary-hub rank stratum. A deterministic implementation obtains \(P\) first and computes every rank, affine, \(W\), and \(C_W\) test from \(P\) alone. R1, R2, and residual cancellation return \(T\) without accessing or validating \(K\); only the observable noncancelling R3 branch reads the predesignated triple for scalar calibration, so malformed or irrelevant triple data cannot alter the cancellation output. A constructed positive noncancelling-R3 pair with binary child ports has identical complete star laws but different sink laws, establishing worst-case need for additional calibration information over the permitted alphabet family; it does not establish pointwise necessity of the designated triple or global design minimality. In the concrete gc-factor encoding, GID-PO has no exact cover and returns no formula. ID-ME separation is not claimed: only skipped EXPAND and the initial exact-cover obstruction are recorded, and all post-initial modules remain an explicit open question.
gap: The dense row gadget is the exact-cover construction used by GID-PO, whose published criterion is sound but not complete. ID-ME adds matrix-equation modules but has no completeness theorem, and its post-initial behavior on these labelled marginal tables has not been resolved. Complete gID and c-gID results use different full-system or \(Q[S]\)-type input contracts. Existing tensor results are generic and rank-restricted. None of these sources states an arbitrary-row, all-rank unknown-hub reconstruction theorem for the concrete star-plus-triple laws.
fill: Prove the normalized piecewise-rational functional \(\Phi\) for every positive compatible rank stratum, give its star-first adaptive implementation, certify the concrete GID-PO exact-cover failure, and construct positive noncancelling-R3 twins showing worst-case star-only nonidentification. Keep the remaining ID-ME trace and maximal-class converse as separate open questions.
